weekly_digest.headline: Industrial autonomy and green methanol gain pace in ports
weekly_digest.editorial: This week confirms two shifts: autonomy is moving from isolated pilots to a port-wide programme, with the Oxa-powered roll-out at Jebel Ali, and electrification is spreading to handling equipment, from Kapalama's all-electric cranes to Manila's hybrid RTGs. Lloyd's Register's report stresses that shipowners are ordering alternative-fuel vessels faster than ports are building the infrastructure; Tuticorin's green methanol hub shows how South Asian ports are responding. Finally, the BCG/TIC4.0 survey shows AI spreading without proof of financial value: impact measurement is becoming the top priority for digital teams.

articles.title: India prepares commercial launch of its first green methanol bunkering hub
articles.summary: V.O. Chidambaranar Port Authority (Tuticorin) announced that India's first dedicated green methanol bunkering hub will start commercial operation at the end of November 2026. The port would become an alternative to Colombo for nearly 80% of ships on the East-West route, building on its status as a green hydrogen hub.
key_points: Commercial operation targeted for end of November 2026
India's first dedicated green methanol bunkering hub
Target: nearly 80% of ships on the East-West route
One of India's three designated green hydrogen hubs
articles.terminal_impact: Worth watching for any carrier or terminal on the East-West route: methanol bunkering supply in India could shift bunkering calls.
articles.criticality_rationale: Imminent start-up of a green methanol bunkering facility, a first in India, on one of the world's main trade lanes.

articles.title: Alternative-fuel ship orders outpace port readiness
articles.summary: Lloyd's Register's "Fuel for Thought: Ports" report counts 1,942 alternative-fuel ships on order (47% of tonnage ordered), while LNG bunkering is available in only 222 ports and methanol in just 25. The first commercial ammonia bunkering took place in Ulsan in April 2026. LR concludes that fuel strategy and commercial strategy are now inseparable.
key_points: 1,942 alternative-fuel ships on order (January 2026)
LNG bunkering: 222 ports; methanol: 25 ports
385 methanol-capable and 45 ammonia-capable ships on order
First commercial ammonia bunkering: Ulsan, April 2026
articles.terminal_impact: Useful benchmark for fuel infrastructure investment decisions: scarce bunkering points create a lasting competitive advantage.
articles.criticality_rationale: Global reference study quantifying the gap between the alternative-fuel fleet and port readiness.

articles.title: NorthPort takes delivery of four hybrid RTGs in Manila
articles.summary: NorthPort, ICTSI's domestic terminal in the Port of Manila, has received four Mitsui E&S hybrid rubber-tyred gantry cranes (RTGs) combining batteries with a downsized diesel engine, each cutting annual CO2 emissions by 58.7% compared with a conventional RTG. The programme includes strengthening Pier 14 and works on Pier 16, due for completion at the end of 2027.
key_points: Four Mitsui E&S hybrid RTGs delivered
-58.7% annual CO2 per unit
Pier 14 strengthening and Pier 16 works
Programme completion at end of 2027
articles.terminal_impact: Useful benchmark for a phased yard equipment upgrade on a brownfield terminal.
articles.criticality_rationale: Deployment of hybrid yard equipment with quantified emission cuts at an operating terminal.

articles.title: IAPH calls for ISPS Code modernisation after global survey
articles.summary: IAPH is leading the modernisation of the ISPS Code twenty years after it came into force: a global survey (181 responses, August-September 2026), submissions to the IMO and a conference debate with more than 700 delegates from 70 countries. The association sees a need for updated guidance against emerging threats, following the US proposal MSC 112/7/1.
key_points: 181 responses to the IAPH global survey (August-September 2026)
Submissions to the IMO; conference with 700+ delegates from 70 countries
Follows US proposal MSC 112/7/1
articles.terminal_impact: Worth watching: an ISPS Code revision would eventually require terminals to update their security set-up.
articles.criticality_rationale: Industry initiative that could lead to a binding revision of the international port security framework.

articles.title: Five all-electric cranes installed at Kapalama Container Terminal
articles.summary: Five all-electric Noell yard cranes were blessed on 5 November at Kapalama Container Terminal (Honolulu), a $555M project by Pasha Group and Hawaii Stevedores. Designed with Hawaiian Electric, the terminal will be able to serve ships without drawing on the public grid, keeping supplies flowing in the event of a natural disaster.
key_points: Five electric Noell cranes installed (blessing on 5 November)
$555M terminal, Hawaii's largest port project
Designed to run off the public grid with Hawaiian Electric
75 m tall units shipped by barge from Long Beach
articles.terminal_impact: Energy resilience model worth studying for terminals exposed to natural hazards: full electrical autonomy of the terminal.
articles.criticality_rationale: Deployment of electric handling equipment and energy autonomy at a major Pacific terminal.

articles.title: DP World rolls out autonomous logistics at Jebel Ali with the SHIFFT JV
articles.summary: DP World becomes the first strategic partner of SHIFFT, a joint venture between the Dubai Future Foundation and autonomy specialist Oxa, to roll out autonomous logistics starting at Jebel Ali, where it runs more than 900 vehicles. The programme covers vehicle integration, safety, fleet management and a digital twin, and could extend to 60 terminals in more than 80 countries.
key_points: DP World is SHIFFT's first strategic partner (DFF + Oxa)
Jebel Ali: more than 900 vehicles in operation
Oxa Driver, Oxa Hub and Oxa Ware systems
Potential extension to 60 terminals in 80+ countries
articles.terminal_impact: Useful reference for scoping an industrial autonomy programme: safety, fleet orchestration and digital twin before deployment.
articles.criticality_rationale: Scale-up of an autonomy programme at the Middle East's leading port, extendable to a global network.

articles.title: Only 4% of port operators can show financial gains from AI
articles.summary: The BCG/TIC4.0 survey of 103 experts shows AI moving beyond trials in container terminals (44% of respondents are scaling up or beyond), but only 4% report measurable bottom-line gains and 11% systematically measure its contribution. Uncertain ROI (41%) and data quality (32%) remain the main barriers.
key_points: 103 experts surveyed (August 2026); 43 use cases assessed
44% scaling up; only 4% with measurable gains
Barriers: uncertain ROI (41%), data quality (32%)
62% exploring document extraction; 48% predictive maintenance
articles.terminal_impact: Build it into the AI roadmap: set up impact measures validated by operations before extending deployments.
articles.criticality_rationale: Convincing figures on the gap between AI adoption and proof of financial value in terminals.

articles.title: Study urges UK ports to move beyond automation pilots
articles.summary: Zenzic, a UK government-backed body, has published a report with WSP on UK port automation: more than 95% of the 120 commercial ports are brownfield sites, steering automation towards mixed, incremental deployments. The study cites the £3.81M deal between PD Teesport and Westwell for autonomous electric terminal tractors.
key_points: Zenzic/WSP report: more than 95% of UK ports are brownfield
Incremental automation rather than full transformation
Teesport: £3.81M for Westwell autonomous electric tractors
Short-distance autonomous drayage identified as the next step
articles.terminal_impact: Worth watching if you run a brownfield terminal: mixed-mode automation and retrofits are becoming an exportable skill.
articles.criticality_rationale: National study setting the framework for scaling automation on existing port sites.

articles.title: Morocco opens the first container terminal at Nador West Med
articles.summary: Nador West Med's East Terminal, the complex's first container terminal, inaugurated on 31 October, has handled its first commercial call. Operated by Marsa Maroc and Terminal Investment Limited (MSC), it offers 1,520 m of quay with 18 m draught and targets 3.5M TEU by 2030; the West Terminal, with CMA CGM, is expected in 2027. The complex represents MAD 54 billion.
key_points: East Terminal inaugurated on 31 October 2026
1,520 m quay; 18 m draught; 3.5M TEU targeted by 2030
Operators: Marsa Maroc and TIL (MSC); West Terminal with CMA CGM in 2027
MAD 54 billion complex (about $5.9 billion)
articles.terminal_impact: New deep-water capacity in the Mediterranean to factor into competitive analysis of Europe-Africa-Asia rotations.
articles.criticality_rationale: Start-up of a major Mediterranean container terminal, changing capacity on Europe-Africa routes.

articles.title: Bilbao delivers the EU report on FuelEU Maritime onshore power supply
articles.summary: The Port Authority of Bilbao led the ESSF working group on the onshore power supply provisions of the FuelEU Maritime regulation; the report was published by DG MOVE. It lists the operational, technical and regulatory difficulties of OPS (short calls, outages, incompatibilities, price swings) and calls for consistent application across the EU.
key_points: Report published by DG MOVE (European Commission)
ESSF working group chaired by the Port of Bilbao
Cases reviewed: short calls, outages, incompatibilities, prices
Balance between operational pragmatism and effective OPS roll-out
articles.terminal_impact: Worth watching for TEN-T network terminals: FuelEU Maritime clarifications will drive the timing of OPS installations.
articles.criticality_rationale: EU regulatory work directly applicable to onshore power supply roll-out.
